## Measured effect
Over the newest **400 real revisions**: **218 of 399** consecutive pairs have an **identical key
set** (so they become byte-identical and produce no commit at all), and when it changes the mean
symmetric difference is **1.78 keys**. Key-set payload at HEAD is **19,960 bytes** vs a **27.1 MB**
full payload.
## Why this is safe — gate G1 was cleared empirically, not by reasoning
A corpus mutation-diff ran the real differ plus the production
`drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` call-site filter over **four real snapshot pairs**
with full prev vs key-set prev and found **zero difference in any observable mutation effect**.
That filter is the load-bearing production guarantee: `run_differs.py` applies it before dispatch
and drops both `(outbound, create, unbound_local)` and `(outbound, update, field_drift)` for either
prev shape. Its removal note remains coupled to a future migration that passes real local state.
Branch-3 also has defense in depth: `_mutation_to_batch_dict` reads
`payload["changed_fields"]` for updates, which branch-3 never sets, so `fields` collapses to `{}`
but the non-parent empty-fields path still invokes a no-op `update_issue(key)`; the load-bearing call-site filter remains the backstop that prevents this branch-3 mutation from reaching dispatch.
**It also removes wasted raw mutations.** With a full prev, keys in prev-but-not-curr make
`compute_mutations` emit 973-998 `(outbound, create, unbound_local)` mutations when the fetch
window shrinks or the project is re-targeted. The existing call-site filter already prevents
those raw emissions from reaching `create_one` at HEAD. A key-set eliminates them at the source,
reducing differ work and mutation-cap pressure without claiming a new Jira-facing behavior change.
Shape constraint: store a **dict** `{jira_key: {}}`, not a `set`. The prev-shape-sensitive
consumers exercised here are `check_dual_identity_complete` and the differ's local-only / emit-both
arms, whose `local_state[key] or {}` guards require mapping entries. The binding walk consumes
`curr_snapshot` and a mutation-derived adopt-skip set, so it is unaffected. On the first pass after
cutover the new reader tolerates an old full-payload prev; the same pass writes the key-set shape,
and the committed full-vs-key-set corpus plus invariant tests cover that coexistence.
## Rollback (mandatory artifact)
The committed corpus runs both forward (full -> key-set) and backward (key-set -> full, the revert
direction) comparisons. Deleting `prev_snapshot.json` is **not** a safe default escape hatch: an
empty prev makes the differ re-derive inbound creates for curr-only keys unless a `rebar-id:` label
suppresses them. If deletion is ever used, it MUST be followed by a cap-0/no-write pass proving
zero unexpected inbound creates.
